A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 20-page versions of SYNTHIA, with corresponding main sections, Appendices A–D, equations, tables and figures. Full-text comparison and visual inspection support reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: V3 reports original image-generation experiments, automatic and human evaluations in Table 1, and ablations and additional results in Section 4.4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V4 retains the original image-generation experiments, automatic and human evaluations, ablations and supplementary results reported in v3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same hierarchical ontology, affordance sampling, three-stage curriculum, contrastive losses and affordance-only inference. Local wording and punctuation edits do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both use the same existing and generated concept-image datasets and task coverage, including two-, three- and four-affordance inputs and close/distant affordance scenarios.

E2.justification: Stable Diffusion, Kandinsky3 and ConceptLab remain in the corresponding comparisons, alongside the same DALL-E comparisons. The newly cited Zhou work is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain 600 training pairs, 500 unseen test pairs, the same evaluation criteria and evaluator models, and the 36-annotator study using 10 sampled pairs. Appendix B protocols and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix C retain the analyses of training-data size, affordance distance, curriculum learning, input complexity, evaluator choice and prompt type, together with the same agreement analyses and visual examples.

E5.justification: Agreement definitions, statistical reporting and human-agreement heatmaps remain identical in Section 4.3 and Appendix C.2. No repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and generated examples match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains SYNTHIA's automatic novelty/coherence scores of 4.55/4.81 and human scores of 3.89/4.06; supplementary result entries are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The ontology, distance definitions and losses in Equations (1)–(5) are unchanged. V4 removes a stray comma between the lines of Equation (1), which corrects punctuation without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about affordance composition, curriculum learning and novel, functionally coherent designs, including the same claimed human-evaluation gains.

C2.justification: Interpretations of baseline behavior, curriculum benefits and generalization are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning subjective novelty evaluation and incomplete ontology coverage.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same prompts, image filtering, baseline versions, hyperparameters, UNet fine-tuning details and reported training time on an NVIDIA A100. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Zhou et al., Contrastive Visual Data Augmentation. The bibliography lists this single work twice as 2025a and 2025b, with identical authors, title and arXiv identifier. Research positioning otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 makes local grammar and phrasing edits in Sections 2–4, corrects equation punctuation and updates the author contact email. The narrative, section order and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V4 removes printed page-number footers and slightly reflows text and references. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–7 retain their structure, captions and placement; embedded figure artwork is identical.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental support, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged throughout both PDFs. Local wording and punctuation fixes provide slight polish, while the newly added citation is duplicated in the bibliography. These limited editorial effects produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
